_comment: Bundle conformance vectors (docs/bundle-format.md §15), computed by scripts/bundle-vectors.py from the spec: each case is built with one stated defect and its expected result declared from that construction. Keys by name; the trust of a case names the keys a verifier is given. Compare the parsed result (§9), never its bytes. `too-large` is not represented: the limits (256 MiB, 10^6 entries) are impractical in a vector file.

cases.name: ok_record_trust_only
cases.note: without checkpoint trust, checkpoints are still checked structurally and counted (§7.6); the erasure is signed, not anchored (§7.9, R6)

cases.name: unauthenticated_no_trust
cases.note: hashes recompute, but nothing establishes provenance (U1)

cases.name: unauthenticated_empty_bundle
cases.note: an empty bundle proves nothing (§9.2)

cases.name: unauthenticated_unanchored_tail
cases.note: checkpoint trust only: the entry after the last checkpoint is not authenticated

cases.name: ok_tail_truncated_to_earlier_checkpoint
cases.note: a chain cut back to an earlier checkpoint verifies: undetectable from the bundle (§1)

cases.name: ok_swapped_inner_entry_id_checkpoint_only
cases.note: a checkpoint does not authenticate inner entry ids; only record signatures do (§1)

cases.name: duplicate_chain
cases.note: every copy keyed by position (§8, §9.3)

cases.name: invalid_chain_id
cases.note: no envelope can be built with an invalid chain id: bad-signature without verifying (§7.7)

cases.name: field_shape_uppercase_hash
cases.note: a malformed entry: not hashed, linked, classified or authenticated; its successor's link is not checked; the checkpoint over it fails binding

cases.name: field_shape_impossible_timestamp
cases.note: the timestamp shape is a real UTC instant, not just a pattern (§4.3)

cases.name: duplicate_entry_id_repeat_malformed
cases.note: the repeat counts whether or not it is itself well-formed (§7.1 step 4, rev 3.1)

cases.name: chain_hash
cases.note: the record envelope does not include chain_hash; the checkpoint binds the tip's stored hash

cases.name: erasure_invalid_relabelled
cases.note: the erasure is found by its hash whatever the label: the events before it stay erased (§7.3)

cases.name: checkpoint_signed_with_context
cases.note: ML-DSA with a non-empty context MUST fail: catches libraries that ignore the context

cases.name: checkpoint_signed_hashml_dsa
cases.note: HashML-DSA MUST fail: proof uses pure ML-DSA

cases.name: checkpoint_signature_out_of_alphabet_record_trust_only
cases.note: the signature's shape is judged in step a, without checkpoint trust too. (3309 bytes need no padding, so an unused-bits variant cannot exist; this is a character outside the alphabet)

cases.name: checkpoint_case_variant_member
cases.note: member names are case-sensitive (Go's decoder folds case)

cases.name: checkpoint_escaped_duplicate_member
cases.note: duplicates are compared after unescaping

cases.name: checkpoint_number_over_2_53
cases.note: JS cannot hold it exactly; refused everywhere

cases.name: record_malformed_signature_alphabet
cases.note: canonical base64 only: no URL-safe alphabet

cases.name: record_signed_by_checkpoint_key
cases.note: the two trust dimensions are separate (§6)

cases.name: record_signature_repeated_hint_index
cases.note: a valid signature re-encoded with a repeated hint index: FIPS 204 Algorithm 21 refuses it

cases.name: disclosed_content_noncanonical_base64
cases.note: non-canonical base64 is a value shape: field-shape, and the event gets no outcome

cases.name: erasure_from_stored_global_seq
cases.note: the erasure hash is built from the predecessor's STORED global_seq (1), not its index (0)

cases.name: erasure_after_malformed_entry
cases.note: an entry whose predecessor is malformed cannot hold the erasure hash (§7.3): E = -1

cases.name: ok_two_erasures
cases.note: E is the LAST erasure; the earlier one is still genuine

cases.name: disclosed_on_erasure
cases.note: a misplaced disclosed is field-shape and the entry's only outcome (§7.1.3): it still holds the erasure hash, so E = 2 and the events before it are erased, but it is not a genuine erasure

cases.name: ok_two_checkpoints
cases.note: checkpoint 1 binds checkpoint 0's anchor chain hash

cases.name: checkpoint_series_second_fails
cases.note: the last PASSING checkpoint decides coverage

cases.name: checkpoint_series_stops_after_failure
cases.note: checkpoint 1 is valid but never checked, and does not count

cases.name: checkpoint_binding_previous_anchor_hash
cases.note: checkpoint 1's anchor chain hash starts from the seed hash instead of checkpoint 0's

cases.name: checkpoint_binding_anchor_chain_hash
cases.note: range right, anchor chain hash wrong, validly signed

cases.name: checkpoint_binding_tip_hash
cases.note: the checkpoint binds the tip's STORED chain hash

cases.name: ok_checkpoint_number_2_53_minus_1
cases.note: the largest number allowed is accepted

cases.name: global_seq_2_63_minus_1_accepted
cases.note: 2^63-1 is in shape (hashed, signed, checkpointed); only the sequence rule objects

cases.name: ok_timestamp_leap_day
cases.note: timestamps are never ordered (temporal authority)

cases.name: ok_disclosed_content_65536_bytes
cases.note: the largest disclosed content allowed

cases.name: ok_malformed_record_signature_without_record_trust
cases.note: without record trust, record_signature members are neither problems nor evidence (§7.7)

cases.name: record_envelope_previous_hash_at_seq_0
cases.note: its signature is a valid ML-DSA-65 signature over that envelope, but no envelope may be built for a non-empty previous hash at sequence 0: bad-signature WITHOUT verifying (§7.7)

cases.name: duplicate_chain_three_extra
cases.note: [A, B, A, B, A]: three extra copies, the first at 2

cases.name: unreadable_json_depth_9
cases.note: top level is depth 1; record_signature's value here reaches 9

cases.name: unreadable_structure_depth_8
cases.note: depth 8 is allowed by the grammar; the wrong type is a structure violation

cases.name: unreadable_precedence_duplicate_key_before_format
cases.note: several reasons: the lowest-numbered is reported

cases.name: unreadable_precedence_format_before_structure
cases.note: the structure violation comes first in the bytes; format still wins

cases.name: unreadable_format_wrong_type
cases.note: a top-level object whose format is not exactly the v1 string, of any type

cases.name: unreadable_json_raw_surrogate_bytes
cases.note: a surrogate encoded as UTF-8 bytes is not valid UTF-8

cases.name: unreadable_precedence_json_before_duplicate_key
cases.note: a duplicate key and a truncation: the JSON reason wins

cases.name: unreadable_structure_number
cases.note: no numbers outside checkpoint text

cases.name: unreadable_structure_number_negative
cases.note: valid RFC 8259 but outside §3's number rule: in the bundle that is a wrong type (§3, rev 3.1)

cases.name: unreadable_structure_number_fraction
cases.note: valid RFC 8259 but outside §3's number rule: in the bundle that is a wrong type (§3, rev 3.1)

cases.name: unreadable_structure_number_exponent
cases.note: valid RFC 8259 but outside §3's number rule: in the bundle that is a wrong type (§3, rev 3.1)

cases.name: unreadable_json_number_plus_sign
cases.note: not RFC 8259 JSON at all

cases.name: unreadable_structure_record_signature_extra_member
cases.note: the members inside record_signature and disclosed are structure (§4.3, rev 3.1)

cases.name: unreadable_structure_record_signature_missing_member
cases.note: the members inside record_signature and disclosed are structure (§4.3, rev 3.1)

cases.name: unreadable_structure_record_signature_number
cases.note: the members inside record_signature and disclosed are structure (§4.3, rev 3.1)

cases.name: unreadable_structure_disclosed_extra_member
cases.note: the members inside record_signature and disclosed are structure (§4.3, rev 3.1)

cases.name: unreadable_structure_disclosed_missing_member
cases.note: the members inside record_signature and disclosed are structure (§4.3, rev 3.1)

cases.name: real_export
cases.note: exported by `proof sink export --disclose all` from a real sink (scripts/bundlefixture); expected result derived from what was built
